description.narrative: " Overall outcome: The establishment of a well-functioning e-GP system in Georgia is expected to result in : (i) increased efficiency and transparency in government procurement at lower cost; (ii) strengthening institutional and regulatory framework; (iii) trained manpower in the use of electronic procurement activities; (iv) improving the perception in the private sector that the Government is serious about addressing or reducing fraud and corruption, principally in the areas of fraudulent practices, misrepresentation, conflicts of interest, and bid-rigging; and (v) reduce fiduciary risks in future public procurement. (a) strengthening of the e-GP legal framework through: (i) review of the current Public Procurement Law related to establishment of e-GP laws and identification of gaps and proposal of solutions; (ii) adaptation of good practices in the area of e-GP to the Georgia context; (iii) consultations with concerned Governmental institutions, private sector, bi-lateral and multilateral donors; and (iv) preparation of amendments in the Public Procurement Law to facilitate the systematic development of e-GP in Georgia; (b) development of institutional mechanisms for e-GP and preparation of technical standards for e-GP, through: (i) assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of existing institutions to carry out e-GP functions; (ii) recommendation of institutional options, organization and management arrangements for carrying out e-GP functions; (iii) consultations with concerned Government institutions and development of a feasible institutional mechanism for carrying out e-GP; (iv) design of a systematic reporting system based on measurable benchmarks with a view to make procurement monitoring more effective; and (v) preparation of detailed technical specifications and standards which will ensure inter-operability between various Government institutions; (c) development of e-GP experts, through: (i) design and development of a training need assessment program based on policy, regulation and technical standards; (ii) preparation of training materials suitable for delivery through face to face and distance learning mechanisms; (iii) provision of intensive training in e-GP systems to selected government employees so that they can function as trainers for other staff; and (iv) provision of hands on training and exposure to working e-GP system in an advanced country (where e-GP is functioning) to selected government specialists. (d) increase of public awareness in procurement reforms and e-GP, including mass media campaigns and dissemination activities, as well as provision of public access to e-GP services."
